correctness.rationale: Every generating derivative equals e₂ on the complement of a (d−2)-index deletion. If a common zero has three distinct coordinate values, delete d−3 indices avoiding them and differentiate e_d to a symmetric cubic; each of its first partials vanishes and equals a common monic quadratic evaluated at the deleted coordinate, contradicting three distinct roots. For exactly two distinct values a,b, let j be the number of a coordinates in each k-subset. If both multiplicities are ≥2 then feasible j includes three consecutive integers, while F(j)=binom(k,2)b²+j(k−1)b(a−b)+binom(j,2)(a−b)² has nonzero second finite difference (a−b)². Thus only singleton exceptional-coordinate points occur. The 0/1 exceptional inclusion equations give b=0 (axis) or p|(k−1) and p|binom(k,2); the latter is exactly Q>2, including char2 condition 4|(k−1), yielding full 2-planes. All-equal coordinates contribute D exactly when p|binom(k,2), whose Q≤2 arithmetic is odd p|k or p=2,4|k. Exhaustion and distinct linear-space dimensions establish the irreducible components of the reduced support, not scheme nilpotents. Independently enumerated the full defining quadratics for all field vectors F₂^n n=4..7, F₃^n n=4..6, F₅^n n=4..5 and every allowed d, comparing to the union formula; no discrepancies. Finite point checks are not proof of algebraic closure result.
